title: DevPilot AI
role: Creator and lead developer: product, frontend, backend, AI integration
summary: A full-stack SaaS product that helps developers get job-ready. It scores resumes against ATS criteria, reviews GitHub projects, runs voice-enabled mock interviews and matches candidates to jobs.
problem: Developers preparing for jobs juggle separate tools for resume checks, portfolio feedback, interview practice and job search, and rarely learn why an application failed.
built: I designed and built the product end to end: a Next.js 16 app with ten dashboard modules, an Express and TypeScript API over MongoDB, real-time interview sessions over Socket.IO, and AI features on Groq's Llama 3.3 70B.
highlights: Next.js 16 · React 19 app with 10 dashboard modules
Express + TypeScript API with 13 route groups
engineering: Layered Express and TypeScript backend (routes, controllers, services, repositories) with 13 API route groups and Zod request validation.
Authentication with JWT and GitHub OAuth through Passport; Helmet, CORS and rate limiting on the API.
Resume pipeline: PDF upload with Multer, text extraction with pdf-parse, then AI analysis for an ATS score and specific fixes.
Live mock interviews: Socket.IO sessions carry questions and answers between the browser and the AI service, with voice input and output in the browser.
GitHub analyzer that pulls repository metadata, README and language data from the GitHub REST API for AI code review.
Weighted Job Ready Score that combines resume, GitHub and skills results into one number with a breakdown.
Swagger/OpenAPI documentation, Winston logging, and Docker Compose for the API and MongoDB.
features: AI coding tools: code generator, bug finder, SQL assistant, documentation writer

title: Production FinTech & Trading Systems
tagline: Live trading terminal, CRM and real-time market data
role: Software Engineer with technical ownership across projects
summary: Professional FinTech work: the RTX 5 Web Terminal traders use in the browser, CRM and back-office workflows, trading analytics, and real-time market-data integrations.
confidentialNote: The trading terminal is public. CRM, back-office and backend code, internal URLs and system details are private and not shown here.
problem: A trading business runs on software that handles real accounts and real money: onboarding and KYC, wallets and transactions, live market data and trading tools. It has to stay correct and available while markets move.
built: I built the frontend of the RTX 5 Web Terminal, a MetaTrader-style trading terminal that runs in the browser. Around it I work across CRM and admin workflows, trading analytics, real-time market data over WebSockets and FIX 4.4, and the production debugging that keeps it running.
highlights: Live: RTX 5 Web Terminal, a browser trading terminal
CRM: accounts, KYC, wallets, deposits, withdrawals
Production debugging across code, servers and gateways
engineering: Frontend of the RTX 5 Web Terminal: streaming quotes, candlestick charts from M1 to MN, one-click trading and account panels, connected to the trading backend over WebSockets.
CRM functionality for users, trading accounts, KYC, wallets, deposits, withdrawals, transactions and admin workflows.
Trading interfaces in React, Next.js and TypeScript: multi-timeframe OHLC charts, symbol switching and live chart updates over WebSockets and FIX 4.4.
Trading-journal analytics: win rate, profit factor, expectancy, risk-to-reward, maximum drawdown, reports, CSV export and Monte Carlo simulation.
Work across PostgreSQL, Prisma, Redis, REST APIs, and Rust, C++ and Node.js components in gateway and trading-system integrations.
Production debugging: HTTP 429/502 errors, authentication, WebSockets, PostgreSQL, Nginx, gateway connectivity and environment configuration.
Investigation of copy-trading execution across the open/close/modify order lifecycle, queues, retries and reconciliation.
Security review that led to server-side validation and clear trust boundaries for a client-trusted check.

title: Aadhaar Mask Detector
tagline: Computer-vision API that masks Aadhaar numbers
role: Solo project: model integration, API, frontend, deployment
summary: Upload an Aadhaar card image and get back a copy with the first eight digits of the number masked, so only the last four stay readable.
problem: Aadhaar cards are routinely shared as ID proof with the full 12-digit number exposed. Masking it by hand is slow and easy to get wrong.
built: A FastAPI service that runs a YOLOv8 model trained to find the number, masks it with OpenCV and returns the result to a drag-and-drop web client. The API is containerised with Docker and runs on Render; the frontend is on Vercel.
highlights: Tesseract OCR for date of birth and gender
engineering: Detection with YOLOv8 (Ultralytics on CPU PyTorch) at 320 px input and a 0.3 confidence threshold, sized for a CPU-only host.
Masking with OpenCV: the first eight digits are covered with the card's sampled background colour and replaced with XXXX XXXX, leaving the last four readable.
Tesseract OCR plus regex parsing to extract date of birth and gender from the card text.
FastAPI upload endpoint with CORS, invalid-image handling and a JSON response carrying the masked image as base64.
Deployment: Dockerfile and a Render blueprint (render.yaml) for the API; static frontend on Vercel.

architecture.note: The masking pipeline, from upload to response.

outcome: Live, with the API on Render and the web client on Vercel.

title: AI Verse
tagline: AI tools for developers and students
summary: A suite of AI tools: chatbot, text summarizer, code explainer and a JavaScript MCQ exam. Version two adds a live HTML/CSS/JS editor with AI code explanation.
problem: Students and developers switch between separate AI tools to explain code, summarise notes and practise questions.
built: Version one is a React app with four AI tools on Gemini 2.0 Flash, PDF input with pdf.js and PDF export with jsPDF. Version two adds a Monaco-based editor with live preview and an Express API that calls Groq's Llama 3.3 70B to explain code.
